note: Every number here traces to PATEL-HANDOFF.md §6/§9, itself sourced from the client's Patel_Retail_data_Munshot.xlsx and Peer_Model.xlsx. Nothing in this file was estimated or invented — derived figures (store EBITDA) are computed at runtime in public/js/economics.js from the reported inputs below, not hardcoded, so the arithmetic stays visible.

unit_economics.sqft_per_store_note: The same 5,000 sq ft blended average applied to all 53 stores uniformly — not a per-store measurement (per-store sq ft was not supplied and isn't coming). Anything derived from this figure inherits the estimate label.

own_brand.note: ₹2.2cr on ~₹449cr retail revenue (~0.5%) — small, but ₹1cr of it sells outside Patel's own stores, which reads as brand behaviour rather than shelf-filling.

private_label_pct.note: Patel's private label is ~2x DMart's, but far below Vishal/Trent — 'very high own-brand' doesn't survive peer context.

revenue_per_sqft_year.resolution_note: The two client files disagree by ~28% on this single most important unit-economics figure. This dashboard uses the store-file value (₹17,280) for every calculation, per instruction — the peer-model figure is shown for reference only, never averaged in and never picked silently.

peer_model_bugs.note: All 10 documented in PATEL-HANDOFF.md §10, from the client's Peer_Model.xlsx. Status is honest per bug: 'fixed' means this dashboard shows the corrected figure below; 'not_applicable' means the bug doesn't carry over because this dashboard doesn't build that metric at all; 'needs_source_file' means the correct value was never given anywhere in the handoff — only that the current one is wrong — and re-opening the original spreadsheet is the only way to fix it.

peer_scale_gap.note: Osia Hyper Retail and V2 Retail are the only peers near Patel's own scale (52 operational stores) — every other peer in the model is 120+ stores. No financial data for either is available in this handoff or anywhere else this session could reach, so no figures are shown for them. Adding real numbers here (revenue, store count, area, EBITDA) is the next step, not a placeholder to fill with an estimate.

store_pnl_reconciliation.flag_note: Building store EBITDA from the client's own per-store unit metrics gives ~5.4% of sales, BEFORE any head-office cost. The peer model claims 7.9% EBITDA at company level for the B2C business — company-level margin cannot exceed store-level once overhead is added. That's backwards as given. Not resolved here (likely causes per the handoff: the 45/55 revenue-based EBITDA split may be the wrong allocation — export probably carries more margin — or the unit-economics inputs are conservative). Surfaced as a flag, not silently fixed.
store_pnl_reconciliation.note: store_ebitda_l / store_ebitda_pct are computed at runtime from the reported inputs above (see public/js/economics.js) rather than stored pre-computed, so the arithmetic stays auditable on screen.
